gap: No result ChatGPT got states which heated 12V batteries heat only from charger current and which can also pre-heat from their own stored energy: LiTime's LiHeat 12V 100Ah and Redodo's Apex Mini 24V 125Ah can do both, while the Redodo 12V 100Ah self-heating, Vatrer 12V 100Ah heated and Renogy Core models heat only from incoming charge, and Renogy sets a floor of more than 10 A of steady charge current per battery.
standout_why: ChatGPT cited the Power Queen self-heating page for a 10 A minimum charge current to start heating, so rivals already have part of this. I could not open that page (TLS certificate error) or the SOK, Battle Born, Renogy DuoHeat and Reserve Power Co. result pages (404 or HTTP 429). None of the 15 result titles mentions pre-heating from battery power. On the maker pages I did read, only LiTime and the Redodo Apex Mini offer it. ChatGPT's answer also treats the heater as a feature every model has, with no split between heating only from the charger and heating from either source.
decides: If the battery charges from a small winter solar array or a weak DC-DC feed, a model that heats only from charger current may never warm up when the current is below the maker's floor (Renogy says more than 10 A per battery). For that shopper the LiTime LiHeat 12V 100Ah Group 24 ($368.99), which can pre-heat from its own stored energy, is the safer pick. If a 20 A or larger AC or DC-DC charger is always available, the Redodo 12V 100Ah self-heating at $251.99 (100 W pads, heat on below 0 °C, off at 5 °C) does the same job for $117 less. Before the page pairs the Redodo with Dealectric's Redodo 14.6V 10A charger, someone needs to open a page that shows Redodo's minimum heating current (see unsourced).
